frontMatter.introduction:
At Skypass Travel Inc (Group), we are committed to providing exceptional travel management services that are efficient, customer-focused, and professionally executed. Our operations span across air ticketing, hotel bookings, ground transfers, travel insurance, visa assistance, and customized travel solutions for leisure, corporate, group, and mission-based travellers. To consistently deliver high-quality service and maintain operational excellence, we recognize the importance of standardized and clearly defined procedures.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual has been developed to ensure that every member of our organization follows a uniform, structured, and well-coordinated workflow. It establishes the guidelines, responsibilities, and protocols necessary to carry out our daily activities effectively, reduce operational errors, and maintain consistency in client experience across all departments.

Through this SOP Manual, we aim to:
Maintain a high level of professionalism, accuracy, and accountability in service delivery
Strengthen coordination between internal teams and external partners
Ensure compliance with industry standards, safety regulations, and ethical business practices
Support employees with clear instructions and role-based responsibilities
Continuously improve our operational efficiency and customer satisfaction

All employees are required to follow the processes outlined in this manual and apply them consistently in their respective roles. This document reflects our culture of excellence and our commitment to providing customers with smooth, reliable, and memorable travel experiences.

We will review and update this manual periodically to ensure that our procedures evolve along with our business, technology, and service expectations. Any revisions will be communicated to all team members in a timely manner.

Together, we uphold the integrity and quality that define Skypass Travel.

blocks.text: The purpose of this Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is to outline Skypass Travel’s structured approach to waste minimization, material efficiency, internal recycling, and environmentally responsible disposal practices. This SOP ensures that waste is managed in a systematic manner to reduce environmental impact, enhance resource utilization, and support sustainable operations.

This SOP applies to all employees, departments, and operational offices of Skypass Travel and covers the handling, segregation, reuse, reduction, recovery, recycling, and disposal of solid waste, electronic waste, hazardous office materials, and general office consumables generated during business activities.

Strategy to minimize waste by reducing material use, reusing products without additional processing, and recycling materials for new applications.
Discarded electronic equipment such as computers, printers, and accessories requiring specialized disposal.
Extracting usable resources from waste to maximize lifespan and reduce environmental burden.

responsibilities: Oversees waste management programs, data tracking, vendor management, and performance reporting.

blocks.text: Internal Waste Minimization & Resource Recovery Program

body.text:
Housekeeping collects packaging materials (cartons, bubble wraps, envelopes, plastic covers, thermocol) daily during waste collection.
Items are placed in the Reuse Material Sorting Table located inside the TWSR.

Admin reuse coordinator inspects materials using Reuse Inspection Checklist (RP-03):
Clean & reusable
Damaged but repairable
Scrap

Wipe/clean all safe-to-reuse items using disinfectant.
Cartons, document holders, and envelopes repaired using basic toolkit.
All approved items are counted and recorded in Reuse Distribution Inventory (RD-06).

Departments request materials through Admin Reuse Portal or Email Form.
First-come/need-based allocation is followed to ensure fair distribution.
Admin logs movement under Reuse Movement Log (RL-07).
Monthly summary of reuse volume, cost savings, and request patterns compiled for ESG dashboard.

82% of packaging requirement met from reuse stock.
Quarterly review identifies non-performing departments.

sections.title: Employee Waste Management Awareness & Capacity Building

blocks.text:
All employees undergo mandatory waste management training during onboarding, emphasizing the importance of reducing, reusing, and recycling.
Regular refresher sessions and quarterly awareness campaigns reinforce employee participation in waste reduction initiatives.
Training includes detailed guidance on segregation practices, labeling requirements, and environmentally safe disposal methods.
Visual aids, info graphics, and signage across office spaces provide constant reminders for proper waste segregation and minimization.
Feedback mechanisms allow employees to suggest new ways to reduce waste, including process adjustments or alternate reusable materials.
HR schedules quarterly training calendar and communicates via email + notice board.
Live training session conducted including:
Demonstration of waste segregation
Use of reuse platform
Examples of incorrect practices
Safety PPE use
Participating employees must sign Training Attendance Register (TR-01).
Staff complete Post-Training Knowledge Assessment Test (min passing: 80%).
Department heads receive monthly compliance scorecards.
Non-performing employees undergo retraining.

body.text: Skypass Travel has established clearly labeled waste segregation stations for paper, plastics, metals, glass, organic waste, e-waste, and general non-recyclable materials.

All Skypass Travel offices operate a 6-Stream Waste Segregation Framework:
Paper/Cardboard
Glass
Metals
Plastic
Organic Waste
Hazardous/Sanitary Waste
E-Waste (Separate)
Segregation bins are color-coded and placed at:
Reception areas
Workstations & open office floors
Pantry rooms & break areas
Printing zones
Near IT service desks
Each bin station includes bilingual signage with examples and QR-coded training resources.
Housekeeping staff collect waste twice daily (10:30 AM & 5:30 PM), documenting volumes using the Daily Waste Recording Log.
Waste is transported via sealed and labeled trolleys to temporary storage rooms.
Waste is handed over to certified disposal vendors as per the disposal schedule:

Vendor Disposal Certificates and Waste Manifests are filed in Waste Compliance Register.
Waste Category & Disposal Method

rows: Collected separately, compacted, and handed over to authorized recycling vendors for pulping and recycling into new paper products.
Segregated by type, stored in dry conditions, and transferred to certified plastic recycling facilities for reprocessing.
Stored in designated metal bins and sent to approved scrap recyclers for melting and reuse.
Collected in impact-resistant containers and handed over to licensed glass recyclers for crushing and remanufacturing.
Disposed of daily through municipal composting facilities or authorized organic waste processors for bio-decomposition.
Collected in sealed, labeled containers and disposed of through authorized incineration or secured landfill as per regulatory norms.
Stored in a secured E-waste storage area and handed over quarterly to government-authorized E-waste dismantlers/recyclers with formal handover certificates.
Disposed of through municipal solid waste management systems and sent to engineered landfills.

blocks.text:
All internal approvals, invoices, itineraries, HR records, and vendor contracts are processed through ERP and cloud-based document management systems, resulting in a significant reduction in paper, printer ink, and physical file storage consumption.
Manual, multi-print approval processes have been replaced with automated digital workflows for travel bookings, reimbursements, and vendor onboarding—eliminating duplicate document generation and reducing stationery usage.
Single-use items such as disposable cups, plastic folders, and single-use cutlery have been eliminated and replaced with reusable mugs, refillable pens, and long-life office organizers across all locations.
Client confirmations, invoices, boarding documents, and travel itineraries are issued electronically as standard practice, minimizing physical print requirements at both office and customer interface levels.
Department-wise consumption data for paper, cartridges, and office consumables is recorded and reviewed monthly by the Operations & Sustainability Team to identify reduction opportunities and process gaps.
Standard operating procedures include inventory optimization; ensuring supplies are purchased based on actual requirement forecasts.
Continuous process improvement initiatives identify opportunities to repurpose excess materials and streamline internal operations.
Departments are encouraged to coordinate and consolidate requirements to reduce redundant ordering and packaging waste.

All paper, envelopes, and notebooks used across Skypass Travel offices are sourced from FSC-certified, recycled, or chlorine-free materials to minimize environmental and health impacts.
All housekeeping operations use biodegradable, non-toxic, and phosphate-free cleaning agents certified under recognized eco-labels to eliminate employee exposure to hazardous substances.
Low-volatile organic compound (VOC) inks, refillable cartridges, and water-based toners are used for printers and office equipment to reduce indoor air pollution and hazardous waste generation.
Compostable cutlery, bio-based packaging, reusable crockery, and paper straws are used in all pantry and food-service areas to eliminate petroleum-based disposables.
IT cables, power strips, insulation materials, and office accessories are procured with RoHS and REACH-compliant specifications to prevent the use of hazardous heavy metals and flame retardants.
All vendors supplying consumables, cleaning chemicals, and pantry materials are screened against eco-compliance criteria including biodegradability, chemical safety data sheets (SDS), and absence of carcinogenic substances.
Liquid soaps, sanitizers, cleaning concentrates, and pantry liquids are procured in bulk refill formats to reduce single-use plastic packaging and hazardous residue waste.
Hazardous material handling inside offices is restricted entirely, with full substitution of chemical-intensive products by bio-based alternatives wherever technically feasible.
Safety Data Sheets for all cleaning and maintenance materials are maintained digitally, and quarterly chemical audits ensure only approved low-hazard materials are in circulation.
Material safety reviews are conducted to progressively replace any remaining moderate-risk materials with bio-based or environmentally superior alternatives.
Employee guidance promotes responsible consumption of materials, ensuring eco-friendly alternatives are properly used and disposed of.

Skypass Travel operates a dedicated internal Inventory Exchange Module integrated with the intranet/ERP system, enabling real-time listing and transfer of surplus office supplies between departments and units.
Each department updates excess or unused materials (paper reams, files, toner, stationery, IT accessories) on the platform with quantity, condition, and location details to enable immediate redistribution.
Employees raise internal requests directly through the platform, which are approved digitally by the respective department admin and fulfilled through centralized stores without new procurement.
The Procurement & Admin Team manages verification, reallocation, and re-issuance of exchanged items to ensure quality control and accurate stock mapping.
Real-time stock visibility of usable surplus materials is available to all business units, preventing duplicate purchases and excess ordering.
No new purchase is approved for commonly reusable items unless the internal exchange platform confirms unavailability across all locations.
Transfer of reusable materials between offices is executed through scheduled logistics runs to minimize transport emissions and ensure efficient redistribution.
Items posted on the platform are inspected for usability and quality before transfer, ensuring functional reuse.
Departments are encouraged to coordinate resource sharing, reducing unnecessary procurement and avoiding premature disposal.
Periodic reminders and communication campaigns promote active participation in the internal exchange system.

sections.title: IT Equipment Reuse and Refurbishment Programme

steps.heading: IT Equipment Reuse and Refurbishment Programme

body.text: The IT department identifies computers, laptops, and peripherals nearing the end of life for refurbishment rather than disposal.

rows: Department Head identifies unused, faulty, slow-performing, or surplus equipment
Equipment is collected and transferred to IT department with acknowledgment
IT updates internal asset register and assigns temporary status “Under Evaluation”

body.text:
Technical Evaluation & Refurbishment Feasibility. Once received, the IT Technician conducts a thorough physical and functional inspection to assess the device’s condition. This includes checking structural components, ports, screens, keyboards, hinges, and power functionality. The evaluation is recorded in the Technical Assessment Checklist.

Following physical inspection, hardware diagnostics are performed using certified benchmarking and health tools to analyze memory, storage, battery condition, motherboard integrity, and network components. Based on diagnostic results, the IT Asset Manager classifies the equipment into one of the following categories:

Category A – Fully Refurbishable: Functionally recoverable with minor repairs or configuration changes.
Category B – Repairable with Parts: Requires replacement components (RAM, SSD, battery, keyboard, display, etc.).
Category C – Spare Parts Harvest: Not usable independently but useful for extracting parts.
Category D – Non-Repairable / E-Waste: Completely obsolete or beyond economical repair.

Following classification, a cost comparison is drafted to evaluate repair versus replacement value. If refurbishment is financially viable, the IT Asset Manager issues approval for refurbishment, documented as an Approval Note, and refurbishment work is scheduled.

Refurbishment Execution. Once approved, refurbishment work is performed by certified IT Technicians. Typical refurbishment activities include SSD/HDD installations or upgrades, RAM expansion, thermal paste replacement, screen or keyboard replacement, battery installation, or other hardware rebuilding steps.

Each refurbished device undergoes performance and load testing to validate reliability, including benchmark performance, battery endurance, thermal stability, and connectivity. If results meet minimum performance standards, the equipment is certified as refurbished and tagged with a Refurbishment Status Label that documents the refurbishment date, model number, technical performance score, warranty period, and next review schedule.

Refurbishment turnaround time typically ranges between 5–7 working days based on parts availability and batch size.

Internal Redistribution & Reallocation of Equipment. Once refurbishment and testing are complete, the asset is transferred to available inventory for internal distribution. Equipment allocation follows a priority framework to ensure optimal resource utilization. Priority is given to:

Temporary or contractual employees and interns
Newly onboarded employees awaiting device assignment
Secondary departments requiring backup equipment
Employees facing operational interruptions due to device failure
Training labs, guest workstations, and meeting room setups

Departments that require equipment must submit an IT Asset Request. The IT Asset Manager reviews the request and selects the appropriate refurbished device based on performance compatibility and operational need. Once approved, the device is physically handed over to the requesting employee, who must sign the Asset Handover Form to confirm receipt and responsibility.

The IT Inventory Controller updates the IT Asset Register with the new assigned status, user name, and location details. After 15 days of use, the user completes the Internal User Feedback Form to evaluate device performance and report any concerns.

Handling Non-Repairable. If equipment is classified as non-repairable or obsolete, it is immediately tagged with a “Beyond Repair / Obsolete” label by the IT Asset Manager and recorded under the E-Waste Inventory Log. The equipment is then transferred to the secure E-Waste Storage Room, which is accessible only to authorized personnel.

Non-repairable IT equipment is stored until the quarterly disposal cycle, during which the Procurement Department and ESG Team coordinate pickup through a licensed, government-approved e-waste recycling vendor. Once collected, the vendor provides an official Environmental Compliance & E-Waste Recycling Certificate, which the ESG Team files in the centralized compliance archive and uploads to the ESG digital repository for audit and statutory verification.

narrative.text:
Skypass Travel conducts monthly tracking of all waste streams, including paper, plastics, e-waste, and organic waste, to measure generation, segregation accuracy, and recycling performance.
Quarterly review meetings are held with the Sustainability & Operations Team and Senior Leadership to evaluate the effectiveness of waste reduction initiatives, internal reuse programs, and refurbishment practices.
Key performance indicators such as volume of waste recycled, percentage of materials reused internally, e-waste refurbishment rates, and reduction in disposable material consumption are analyzed to inform improvement strategies.
Monitoring results, internal audit findings, and employee feedback are used to update waste management processes, enhance training programs, and optimize internal material exchange systems, ensuring continuous improvement and compliance with environmental goals.

sops.title: Environmental Awareness and Sustainable Travel Initiatives

blocks.text: The purpose of this SOP is to outline the strategies and practices Skypass Travel has implemented to promote environmental awareness, sustainable travel, and responsible choices among its customers. This includes initiatives to reduce carbon emissions, encourage eco-friendly behaviors, and integrate environmental considerations into services and offerings.
This SOP applies to:

All customer-facing services and offerings provided by Skypass Travel, including travel packages, tours, office facilities, and digital platforms.
All employees, guides, and contractors involved in service delivery or customer engagement.
Activities that influence customer environmental impact, including travel options, catering, transportation, and sustainability advocacy.

rows.definition: Total greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions generated directly or indirectly by a product, service, or activity.
Travel practices that minimize environmental impact, including reduced emissions, responsible resource use, and conservation of natural habitats.
Modes of travel such as bicycles, electric vehicles, public transport, or walking that reduce reliance on private, fossil-fuel-powered vehicles.
Disposable plastic items intended for one-time use, such as bottles, cups, cutlery, and straws.

responsibilities: Approve environmental service policies, review progress, and allocate resources for advocacy programs.
Implement environmental initiatives, coordinate eco-friendly service options, and monitor customer adoption.
Educate customers on sustainable options, promote low-impact choices, and facilitate eco-friendly services.
Ensure on-site environmental practices are followed, advise customers on nature impacts, and maintain sustainable service standards.

body.text:
Skypass Travel provides tools and services that allow customers to calculate the carbon footprint of their travel, including flights, transport, accommodations, and activities.
Customers are provided with personalized recommendations to offset emissions or choose lower-impact alternatives.
Carbon footprint data is integrated into booking confirmations, reports, and travel summaries to increase awareness of environmental impact.
The company encourages optional carbon offset programs, including tree planting or renewable energy contributions, aligned with customer travel choices.
Information on booking confirmations link to a personalized carbon dashboard showing emissions per flight, hotel stay, and transport.
Customers can choose "eco-friendly trip" filters that automatically select lower-emission flights and hotels.

We provide our customers with tools to understand and reduce the carbon footprint of their travel.

How We Implement This:

Customers can share trip details with us, including transportation modes, accommodation choices, and selected activities.
Using internationally recognized standards (GHG Protocol, ISO 14064), we calculate the carbon footprint for each trip, providing a clear, easy-to-understand report.
The report highlights the highest contributors to emissions and suggests ways to reduce or offset them.

How Customers Benefit:

Customers receive actionable insights to make eco-friendly choices, such as low-emission travel options or selecting eco-certified accommodations.
We also provide options for verified carbon offsetting directly through our platform.

Our Commitment to Improvement:

We continuously monitor participation and customer feedback, reviewing our carbon calculation methods annually to ensure accuracy and usability.

steps.heading: Provision of Plant-Based Food & Beverage Options

body.text:
All travel packages, tours, and office catering options include plant-based or vegetarian alternatives to reduce environmental impact.
Menus highlight low-carbon footprint food choices, providing customers with clear information to make sustainable selections.
Catering partners are selected based on sustainability certifications and eco-friendly practices, ensuring responsible sourcing of ingredients.
Periodic customer surveys gauge acceptance and satisfaction with plant-based options, informing menu adjustments and sustainability communication.

We actively promote plant-based meals and beverages as part of our commitment to reducing the environmental footprint of travel.

Our Approach:

All Skypass tours and partner accommodations offer clearly labeled plant-based options.
We collaborate with suppliers and chefs to ensure these options are nutritious, culturally relevant, and appealing to all customers.

Customer Engagement:

Menus, apps, and promotional materials highlight the environmental benefits of plant-based meals, encouraging customers to make sustainable food choices.

Monitoring and Feedback:

We track the selection of plant-based options and gather customer feedback to continuously improve variety, taste, and overall satisfaction.

Skypass Travel has introduced reusable water bottles, coffee cups, and food containers for customer use during tours and office interactions.
Plastic straws, cutlery, and packaging materials have been replaced with compostable or reusable alternatives.
Customers are educated on refill stations, proper cleaning, and sustainable disposal practices during tours.
On tours, all disposable cutlery replaced with bamboo sets, and used items collected for sterilization.
Periodic audits track single-use plastic reduction rates and identify opportunities for further improvement.

Our Actions:

We provide reusable water bottles, containers, and eco-friendly packaging for meals and travel kits.
Customers are encouraged to bring their own containers through incentive programs such as discounts or loyalty points.

Maintenance and Hygiene:

Reusable items are collected, cleaned, and sanitized according to strict hygiene protocols to ensure safety.
We monitor reductions in single-use plastic consumption and measure customer participation in our reusable container programs.

Travel packages prioritize electric or hybrid vehicles for transfers and local tours wherever feasible.
Customers are encouraged to adopt alternative modes of transportation, including bicycles, shared shuttle services, and public transport options.
Travel itineraries highlight low-emission routes and sustainable mobility solutions, reducing the reliance on private fossil-fuel vehicles.
All airport transfers in top 5 city tours are done using electric vans; hybrid cars used elsewhere.
App provides "green route" suggestions for customers taking local taxis or shuttles.
Partner hotels provide charging stations; bookings include a note on EV-friendly properties.

Our Implementation:

Skypass partners with electric vehicle rental services, bike-sharing programs, and public transportation providers.
Charging stations are made available at key partner hotels and tour hubs where feasible.

Customer Engagement:

Sustainable travel options are prominently highlighted on our booking platform, mobile app, and pre-trip communications.
Customers receive incentives, such as loyalty points or discounts, for choosing low-emission transportation.
We track usage patterns and assess the effectiveness of our initiatives to continuously enhance customer uptake and environmental impact.

steps.heading: Consideration of Nature Impacts During Tours

body.text:
All tours are planned to minimize environmental impact, including limiting the number of visitors in sensitive areas and avoiding activities that harm wildlife or natural habitats.
Guides educate customers on conservation practices, responsible behavior, and Leave No Trace principles during excursions.
Environmental impact assessments are conducted for new tour routes or experiences, ensuring sustainability considerations are integrated from planning to execution.
Customer feedback is collected on eco-conscious practices, enabling continuous improvement in environmental advocacy initiatives.

All tour itineraries are designed to reduce waste: reusable meal kits, refillable water stations, and digital tickets replace paper.
Light and noise pollution is minimized in wildlife-sensitive areas through controlled lighting, quiet travel zones, and electric/hybrid vehicles.
Water use is optimized during accommodations and activities, with hotels and lodges participating in water-saving programs.
Partnerships with local conservation NGOs enable tree planting, habitat restoration, and biodiversity monitoring programs linked to tours.
Eco-certified accommodations and local businesses are prioritized in bookings to support sustainable operations and community resilience.
Selected tours include optional volunteering experiences such as beach clean-ups, mangrove restoration, or wildlife monitoring.
Pre-trip digital guides and short videos educate customers about local ecosystems, endangered species, and responsible behavior.
Tour guides conduct on-site awareness briefings about biodiversity, pollution prevention, and cultural respect.
Customers are incentivized to adopt low-impact behaviors through loyalty points, recognition badges, or discounts on eco-friendly activities.

narrative.text:
Skypass Travel monitors the adoption of sustainable travel options, including electric vehicle bookings, alternative transportation usage, and plant-based catering choices, on a monthly basis.
Quarterly reviews are conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of single-use plastic reduction, carbon footprint calculation programs, and customer participation in environmental initiatives.
Key performance indicators (KPIs) such as percentage of low-carbon travel options selected, single-use plastic reduction, number of customers using carbon offset programs, and plant-based meal adoption are tracked to assess impact.
Feedback from customers, tour guides, and partners is analyzed regularly to refine environmental advocacy programs, update SOPs, and ensure continuous improvement in promoting sustainable practices.

blocks.text: The purpose of this SOP is to define structured measures adopted by Skypass Travel to protect the health and safety of customers during all interactions, transactions, and service experiences. The procedure ensures risks to customers are proactively identified, monitored, and mitigated, and that customers can provide feedback or report concerns through a responsive, structured system.
This SOP applies to:

All customer-facing operations of Skypass Travel, including offices, digital services, and travel assistance platforms.
All employees and contractors interacting with customers or handling customer information.
Systems, processes, and infrastructure used to identify, assess, and mitigate customer health and safety risks.

rows.definition: The protection of customers from physical, psychological, or environmental risks during their engagement with company services.
A structured process to identify, evaluate, and mitigate potential hazards that may impact customer safety.
A set of planned procedures and resources in place to respond efficiently to incidents affecting customer safety.
Channels through which customers can report concerns, complaints, or suggestions regarding health and safety.

responsibilities: Approve customer health and safety policies, review incident reports, and ensure sufficient resources for safety programs.
Implement health and safety procedures, manage the dedicated hotline, and respond to customer feedback promptly.
Conduct regular risk assessments, maintain emergency equipment, and monitor compliance with safety procedures.
Adhere to health and safety protocols, report hazards or incidents, and assist in emergency procedures when necessary.

body.text:
Skypass Travel maintains a dedicated hotline and email channel specifically to handle customer health and safety concerns, complaints, or suggestions.
All incoming feedback is logged into a centralized tracking system that records the nature of the concern, priority level, and follow-up actions.
Reports are reviewed daily by the Customer Experience Team, and urgent issues are escalated immediately to management for resolution.
Customers receive acknowledgment and response timelines, ensuring transparency and accountability.

We operate a 24/7 dedicated health and safety hotline, accessible via phone, email, and our mobile app.
Hotline information is shared during booking confirmation, pre-travel emails, and on our mobile app.

Staff receives specialized training in first aid, emergency triage, crisis communication, and escalation procedures.
