body.text:
A. Submission Methods: Feedback can be submitted through multiple channels including email, company website, hotline, or social media platforms. All submissions are directed to the Health & Safety Officer within 24 hours of receipt.

B. Confidentiality: All submissions are treated with strict confidentiality. Anonymity is maintained upon request.

C. Response Timeline

Acknowledgment: Within 24 hours of submission
Initial Review: Within 48 hours
Resolution: Based on severity, typically within 3–10 working days

Every feedback entry is recorded in the External Feedback Register (EFR), a secure digital database.
Each record contains: date of submission, source, summary of issue, severity, location, response actions, and final resolution.
A Unique Tracking Number (UTN) is generated for monitoring and follow-up.
Access is restricted to authorized Health & Safety personnel only.

Review Window: All feedback is assessed within 48 hours by the Health & Safety Officer.
Classification:
Urgent: Requires immediate intervention (e.g., safety hazards in public areas).
Non-Urgent: Tracked and addressed according to standard timelines.
Prioritization: Determined based on potential impact, reputational risk, and regulatory or legal implications.
A. Urgent Issues

A cross-functional team (HR, Facilities, Security) is assembled immediately.
Immediate measures are taken, such as restricting access, providing medical support, or repairing faulty equipment.
An incident report is prepared within 48 hours.
Transparent communication is maintained with the feedback provider throughout the process.
B. Non-Urgent Issues

The relevant department head leads the investigation.
A Corrective Action Plan (CAP) is developed, outlining tasks, timelines, and accountability.
The feedback provider is regularly updated until the issue is resolved.
A post-resolution evaluation is conducted to confirm closure and effectiveness of actions.

Customers report emergencies, seek medical guidance, or clarify safety protocols.
Agents provide immediate instructions, coordinate with local medical services, and escalate urgent cases to management or authorities.

All hotline interactions are logged in a centralized incident management system.
Data includes customer details, type of incident, actions taken, resolution time, and follow-up requirements.
Weekly and monthly reports track response times, issue resolution, and recurring patterns.
Insights inform staff training, procedural updates, and communication improvements.

Skypass Travel has implemented a comprehensive emergency response framework covering physical locations, digital platforms, and customer interactions. Detailed evacuation plans, assembly points, first-aid kits, and emergency contact lists are maintained and regularly updated.

Risk-Specific Planning: We develop detailed emergency protocols for:

Medical emergencies (injury, illness, allergic reactions)
Natural disasters (storms, earthquakes, floods)
Security incidents (theft, political unrest)
Accidents during travel or activities
Staff Preparedness:

All tour guides and operational staff receive annual training in first aid, CPR, and emergency evacuation.
Designated Emergency Response Officers coordinate internal and external support during incidents.
Emergency Equipment & Resources:

First aid kits and AED devices are available on all tours, vehicles, and key facilities.
Partnerships with local hospitals, clinics, and ambulance services ensure rapid response.
Customers receive pre-trip emails, app notifications, and in-person briefings covering:
Emergency contacts
Evacuation routes and procedures
Safety precautions for specific destinations or activities
Testing & Drills:

Emergency response procedures are tested quarterly via simulations and drills.
Post-drill reports identify gaps, assign corrective actions, and update procedures.

Regular risk assessments are conducted to proactively identify potential health or safety hazards affecting customers in office spaces, service interactions, or travel-related advisory operations. Hazards are evaluated based on severity and likelihood, and preventive or mitigation measures are implemented accordingly. Risk assessment reports include recommendations for operational adjustments, infrastructure improvements, or policy updates to reduce exposure.

Risk Identification:

For each trip, we evaluate:

Transportation risks (vehicles, modes, road conditions)
Activity risks (trekking, water sports, adventure activities)
Environmental risks (weather, altitude, wildlife)
Local health risks (infectious diseases, food safety)

Risk Assessment Documentation:

All hazards are assessed for likelihood and impact using a standardized risk matrix.
Mitigation measures are documented for each identified risk.

Mitigation Measures:

Examples include:

Requiring personal protective equipment (helmets, life jackets)
Providing sanitation kits and hand hygiene facilities
Partnering with certified accommodation providers for fire and health safety compliance
Limiting participant numbers in high-risk activities
Risk assessments are prepared by the Health & Safety Team in collaboration with tour managers and operational staff.
Assessments are reviewed and approved by senior management before tour launch.
Risk assessments are updated annually or whenever new activities, destinations, or regulations emerge.

Customers are provided with clear guidance on health and safety protocols, including signage in offices, safety guidelines on digital platforms, and instructions during service interactions. Communication channels are continuously updated to reflect current health advisories, local regulations, and emergency procedures.

Pre-Travel Communication:

Customers receive detailed guidance via email, app notifications, and brochures, including:

Vaccination and medical advice
Safety tips for activities and destinations
Emergency contacts and procedures
On-Trip Awareness:

Tour guides provide safety briefings at the start of each activity.
Customers are reminded of hygiene practices, social distancing (where applicable), and protective equipment requirements.
Signage and in-app alerts reinforce safety measures in hotels, vehicles, and tour sites.
Education & Engagement:

Customers can participate in workshops or webinars covering:
Travel health tips
Emergency preparedness
Local environmental hazards
We promote awareness of personal responsibility and adherence to safety guidelines.
Customers are encouraged to share feedback on safety experiences through post-trip surveys.
Feedback informs continuous improvement initiatives.

All incidents, near-misses, and customer complaints are analyzed monthly to identify trends and systemic issues.
The SOP and related safety procedures are periodically reviewed and updated based on incident analysis, risk assessments, and feedback.
Lessons learned are incorporated into employee training modules, emergency drills, and customer guidance materials to strengthen safety outcomes.
KPIs related to customer safety, including response time to complaints, incident resolution rates, and risk mitigation effectiveness, are monitored and reported to senior management quarterly.
Best practices and new technologies in customer safety management are evaluated for potential implementation, ensuring continuous enhancement of protective measures.

narrative.text:
Skypass Travel conducts monthly monitoring of all customer safety incidents, hotline reports, and feedback submissions to track the nature, frequency, and resolution of issues.
Quarterly reviews are carried out by the Sustainability & Operations and Customer Experience Teams to evaluate the effectiveness of emergency preparedness procedures, risk mitigation measures, and response times.
Key performance indicators (KPIs) such as incident resolution rate, average response time to safety concerns, number of near-miss events, and risk assessment completion are analyzed to ensure compliance with internal safety standards.
Findings from monitoring activities, internal audits, and customer feedback are used to update SOPs, improve staff training, and refine emergency response protocols, ensuring continuous improvement in customer health and safety practices.

blocks.text: The purpose of this SOP is to establish structured guidelines and operational practices implemented by Skypass Travel to reduce overall energy consumption and minimize greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across all business activities. This procedure supports the company’s sustainability commitments, enhances operational efficiency, and contributes to global climate action by adopting responsible energy management.
This procedure applies to:

All offices and operational locations of Skypass Travel.
All employees, contractors, and service partners.
All administrative, IT, and facility management activities where energy resources are consumed.
All travel-related consulting operations involving digital systems and workplace infrastructure.

rows.definition: Heat-trapping gases including carbon dioxide (CO₂), nitrous oxide (N₂O), methane (CH₄), and refrigerant gases.
A structured evaluation of energy performance to identify reduction opportunities and set improvement goals.
Total amount of power used by electrical, mechanical, IT, and office systems within operational control.
Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning systems used to regulate indoor temperatures and air quality

responsibilities: Approve energy policies, performance targets, infrastructure upgrades, and annual review outcomes
Develop strategy, review performance data, oversee implementation, lead improvement planning
Apply energy-saving measures across lighting, HVAC, appliances, and building maintenance
Optimize energy usage of IT infrastructure, enforce sleep-mode policies, manage hardware upgrades and virtualization
Coordinate awareness programs and training modules for employee engagement
Conduct periodic audits, verify compliance, and prepare improvement recommendations
Follow daily energy-saving practices, shut down devices, comply with operational instructions, report wastage

body.text:
Skypass Travel has deployed digital energy monitoring systems, including sub-metering across operational zones, enabling real-time visibility of consumption trends and peak-load behavior.
Energy performance statistics are reviewed every month by the Sustainability and Operations Team through analytical dashboards that highlight irregular usage or equipment-related inefficiencies.
Insights from collected data are translated into improvement action plans, which may include equipment upgrades, optimization of operating schedules, or procedural adjustments.
A consolidated quarterly evaluation report is submitted to senior leadership outlining progress, deviations, and recommended improvement measures to support continuous sustainability management.
Benchmark comparisons are conducted with industry standards and historical performance to identify long-term reduction opportunities.
Data-based performance findings are integrated into annual sustainability strategy planning, ensuring that future initiatives are aligned with measured results.

All Skypass Travel facilities have undergone a systematic transition to LED lighting with low wattage configurations, replacing traditional lighting fixtures as part of an energy modernization commitment.
Occupancy-based motion sensors and automatic dimming features are installed in low-use spaces such as corridors, storage areas, restrooms, and shared meeting rooms to eliminate unnecessary lighting load.
Office architectural layouts are intentionally designed to maximize access to natural daylight, reducing dependency on artificial lighting and supporting employee comfort.
Sensor-based lighting systems (motion and occupancy sensors) are installed across low-use areas to ensure automatic on/off control.
Daylight sensor–controlled lighting is deployed near windows to automatically reduce artificial lighting during daytime.
Smart timer-based lighting panels are installed to automatically switch off non-essential lights after office hours.
The Facilities Team carries out routine quarterly assessments to verify lighting system efficiency, document findings, and apply corrective actions where early deterioration or faults are detected.
Timed lighting controls automatically power off office lighting after business hours, preventing avoidable night-time energy consumption.
All lighting upgrades are approved only after lifecycle energy-cost and carbon-reduction assessments to ensure long-term financial and environmental performance.

High-efficiency HVAC equipment with modern inverter technology has been deployed across all office sites, replacing outdated and energy-intensive units.
Smart temperature control systems maintain optimized indoor climate settings, with programmed operation tied to occupancy and working hours to avoid unnecessary cooling loads.
Maintenance performance and energy impact data are digitally logged and reviewed during monthly sustainability review meetings, enabling benchmarking against baseline usage figures.
Workspace insulation and reflective blinds have been installed to reduce indoor heat gain, lowering dependency on cooling operations.
HVAC scheduling ensures systems are shut down outside working hours, and standby mode is used during low activity periods to prevent over-running.
Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) 4-star and 5-star rated inverter split air conditioners are installed across all operational office areas.
Digital thermostat–controlled temperature systems are used to maintain standardized cooling settings during office hours.

Office machinery and appliances such as printers, multifunction devices, and pantry equipment are procured strictly based on energy efficiency certification standards including ENERGY STAR and equivalent national benchmarks.
Default device configurations are pre-set to sleep mode and automatic shutdown features, minimizing idle-time energy consumption during non-operational hours.
Employees are instructed and routinely reminded to adopt shared-use practices and shut down equipment when not in use.
ENERGY STAR–rated printers and scanners with auto sleep mode are used in daily operations.
Smart power extension boards with on/off switches are used at workstations to control idle power use.
High-efficiency UPS systems are installed for computers and networking equipment to reduce standby losses.
Administrative teams conduct periodic compliance inspections and identify outdated equipment for scheduled replacement based on energy performance requirements.

steps.heading: IT Systems and Digital Energy Efficiency

body.text:
Skypass Travel’s IT infrastructure uses high-efficiency hardware and optimized data center cooling to reduce carbon intensity associated with digital systems.
Cloud-based reservation, accounting, and document management systems are used to reduce dependence on on-site servers.
Automatic sleep, hibernation, and shutdown settings are enabled on all company laptops and desktops.
Energy-efficient Wi-Fi routers, network switches, and access points are installed for daily IT connectivity.
Extensive virtualization and cloud migration initiatives have been implemented, significantly reducing on-premise server requirements and energy demand.
IT performance and power consumption are tracked through Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) indicators, which are reviewed quarterly to guide improvement decisions.
Company-issued computers operate under pre-set automatic hibernation and shutdown protocols, and employees are educated on responsible digital usage to limit unnecessary system loads.
Data storage is optimized through automated archival processes and reduced redundant data retention, decreasing server energy demand.
Periodic employee campaigns and digital efficiency drives promote responsible computing habits, including reduction of unnecessary processing workloads.

Procurement policies incorporate energy-efficiency performance criteria for every purchase category, including IT hardware, building systems, lighting components, and support appliances.
Vendors are evaluated on their sustainability credentials and adherence to energy efficiency standards before contract finalization.
Agreements include mandatory environmental compliance clauses, and suppliers undergo evaluation reviews to ensure consistent alignment with Skypass Travel’s sustainability objectives.
Vendor sustainability performance is included as part of annual vendor scorecard assessments, supporting progressive supply chain improvement.
Preference is given to suppliers who implement renewable energy, carbon-neutral logistics, environmentally responsible packaging, or green certification commitments.

All employees participate in mandatory energy efficiency and climate-action learning programs, strengthening organization-wide awareness and accountability for shared sustainability goals.
Training content includes practical guidelines for daily workplace actions, internal real-world case examples, and best-practice examples for reducing energy consumption and GHG emissions.
Training completion and refresher timelines are monitored through Skypass Travel’s Learning Management System (LMS), with attendance and certification records retained for audits and reporting requirements.
Communication campaigns and awareness drives reinforce behavioral practices that collectively support the company’s environmental commitments.

We are actively exploring opportunities for renewable energy adoption, including solar power and green electricity sourcing, with the expected outcome of reducing long-term electricity-related carbon emissions and dependence on grid-based fossil fuels.
The organization is in the process of evaluating structured carbon auditing mechanisms to assess current emission profiles, with the expected outcome of establishing a reliable baseline for future emission reduction planning and regulatory alignment.
Carbon offset options through verified international programs are being explored to address residual emissions, with the expected outcome of enabling future carbon-neutral operations for unavoidable emission sources.

narrative.text:
Skypass Travel conducts monthly monitoring of energy consumption across all office locations using smart meters and internal analytics dashboards to track usage trends and identify abnormal consumption patterns.
Quarterly performance reviews are carried out by the Sustainability & Operations Team and reported to Senior Leadership, including progress against reduction targets, corrective measures taken, and opportunities for improvement.
Key performance indicators such as total electricity usage, energy intensity per employee, HVAC efficiency metrics, and estimated GHG reduction outcomes are continuously assessed to evaluate the impact of implemented initiatives.
Findings from monitoring activities, internal audits, and equipment inspection reports are used to update action plans and refine operational strategies, ensuring continuous improvement and alignment with long-term sustainability goals.

blocks.text: The purpose of this SOP is to establish systematic guidelines and operational practices implemented by Skypass Travel to optimize water usage, prevent wastage, and ensure responsible management of water resources across all business activities. This procedure supports the company’s sustainability commitments, strengthens operational efficiency, and contributes to water stewardship and environmental conservation.
This procedure applies to:

All offices, branches, and operational locations of Skypass Travel.
All employees, contractors, and service partners.
All administrative, IT, and facility operations where water is consumed.
All travel-related consulting operations involving office infrastructure, guest services, and hygiene facilities.

rows.definition: The practice of reducing water consumption while maintaining operational functionality.
Wastewater generated from sinks, showers, and office activities that can be treated and reused for non-potable purposes.

responsibilities: Approve water management policies, targets, infrastructure upgrades, and review outcomes annually
Develop strategy, analyze water consumption data, oversee implementation, lead improvement planning
Implement water-saving measures in plumbing, HVAC cooling, and hygiene facilities; maintain water systems
Ensure digital operations support water efficiency indirectly, e.g., cloud adoption reducing onsite cooling water needs
Conduct employee awareness programs and training on water conservation practices
Audit water usage compliance, verify effectiveness of measures, and provide recommendations
Follow water-saving practices, report leaks or wastage, and adhere to operational guidelines

steps.heading: Water Usage Monitoring and Performance Assessment

body.text:
Smart water meters and digital monitoring systems are installed across all locations to track real-time water consumption trends.
Monthly water usage reports are reviewed by the Sustainability & Operations Team to identify irregular consumption patterns and potential inefficiencies.
Data insights inform operational improvements, such as fixture upgrades, leak repairs, and procedural adjustments.
Quarterly performance reports are submitted to senior leadership, detailing usage trends, corrective actions, and progress toward conservation targets.

Low-flow faucets, dual-flush toilets, and sensor-based taps are installed across all office and public areas.
Automated water control systems are deployed in restrooms and pantry areas to minimize unnecessary usage.

All employees participate in mandatory water conservation training, including practical guidance on daily office actions and water-efficient habits.
Awareness campaigns are conducted via internal newsletters, posters, and digital communications to reinforce water-saving behaviors.
Employees are encouraged to report leaks, dripping faucets, or inefficient appliances through internal reporting channels.
Usage guidelines, such as limiting excessive toilet flushing or sink use, are communicated as part of operational best practices.
Procurement policies include water-efficiency criteria for equipment such as dishwashers, HVAC cooling systems, and plumbing fixtures.

Water consumption is monitored monthly via smart meters and analyzed for abnormal patterns or inefficiencies.
Quarterly reviews by the Sustainability & Operations Team evaluate performance against reduction targets and identify corrective actions.
KPIs such as total water usage, water per employee, efficiency of plumbing fixtures, and recycled water volume are continuously tracked.
Findings from monitoring, audits, and inspections inform updates to operational procedures, ensuring continuous improvement and alignment with sustainability goals.

sops.title: Inclusive Sourcing & Non-Discrimination in the Supply Chain

blocks.text: The purpose of this SOP is to establish and implement actions that ensure Skypass Travel’s supply chain is fair, ethical, inclusive, and free from discrimination, harassment, or any human rights violations. This SOP supports responsible procurement practices that promote equal opportunities for suppliers and protect workforce rights throughout the supply chain.

All suppliers, contractors, service providers, agents, and business partners of Skypass Travel.
All employees involved in procurement, vendor onboarding, vendor evaluation, and contract negotiations.
All outsourcing activities and third-party vendor engagements linked to travel services, logistics, marketing, IT, and operations.

rows.definition: Procurement practices that prioritize suppliers owned or led by underrepresented groups and ensure fair access without discrimination.
Ensuring equal opportunities regardless of gender, age, caste, religion, disability, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or socioeconomic status.
Standards suppliers must follow related to ethics, labor rights, non-discrimination, safety, and environmental practices.

responsibilities: Approves and oversees inclusive sourcing strategies and policy compliance.
Executes supplier evaluation, onboarding, audits, and compliance reviews.
Ensures contractual enforcement and handles violation cases or escalations.
Comply with Skypass Travel’s Supplier Code of Conduct and non-discrimination standards.

blocks.text: Skypass Travel follows a structured Inclusive Procurement Framework designed to ensure equitable access to business opportunities and selection of suppliers based on ethical, social, and sustainability criteria in addition to cost and quality. Key implementation actions include:

body.text:
Prioritizing engagement with suppliers from diverse and underrepresented groups, including women-owned, minority-owned, MSME, startup, and local community-based enterprises.
Requiring suppliers to complete comprehensive registration and onboarding documentation, including disclosures related to ownership structure, labor and human rights practices, workplace diversity initiatives, and compliance certifications.
Using objective vendor evaluation scorecards that incorporate social responsibility performance, workplace policies, fair wage commitments, labor standards compliance, and DEI (Diversity, Equity & Inclusion) initiatives.
Conducting pre-qualification assessments and screening to ensure suppliers uphold equal opportunity employment, non-discriminatory recruitment, and ethical labor standards in alignment with international frameworks such as the UN Guiding Principles on Business & Human Rights (UNGPs) and ILO Conventions.

steps.heading: Prevention of Discrimination & Harassment in Supply Chain Workforce

body.text: To ensure a safe, fair, and respectful working environment across the supply chain, Skypass Travel enforces strict expectations on supplier conduct and compliance. Implementation measures include:

Mandatory acceptance of the Skypass Travel Supplier Code of Conduct, prohibiting discrimination, harassment, retaliation, child labor, forced labor, unsafe workplaces, and any violation of human dignity.
Requiring suppliers to implement formal internal grievance systems accessible to all employees without risk of retaliation or penalties.
Conducting annual supplier audits and compliance reviews, including document verification, physical site inspections, employee interviews, and assessments of policy effectiveness.
Issuing Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) in case of identified risks or violations, with defined timelines and monitoring for improvement. Suppliers who fail to comply face suspension, reduced engagement, or contract termination.
Skypass Travel is committed to enhancing supplier capabilities and strengthening ethical practices across the value chain.
Training Programs:

Suppliers are enrolled in mandatory capacity-building sessions, covering topics such as:
Environmental management and energy efficiency practices
Health, safety, and labor standards
Ethical procurement and anti-corruption guidelines
Digital and operational best practices for sustainability
Delivery Modes:

Training is delivered through virtual workshops, on-site sessions, and e-learning modules for flexibility and accessibility.
Programs are tailored to supplier size, operational context, and strategic importance.
High-impact suppliers (critical to operations or with high environmental footprint) receive intensive and specialized training.
Evaluation & Certification:

Supplier participation is tracked, and completion certificates are issued upon successful completion of training modules.
Supplier knowledge and capability improvements are assessed through quizzes, audits, and practical demonstrations.

To support transparency and fair conflict resolution, Skypass Travel offers grievance channels accessible to suppliers and their employees. Maintaining a dedicated Supplier Support & Grievance Mechanism available through hotline, email, and online reporting forms to confidentially raise concerns related to discrimination, harassment, or unethical labor practices.
Grievance Channels:

Suppliers can report grievances via:
Dedicated email addresses
Supplier portals in our digital management system
Direct contact with the Supplier Relationship Manager
Issues may include contractual disputes, compliance concerns, ethical or labor practice questions, or operational conflicts.
Acknowledgement & Tracking:

All grievances are acknowledged within 48 hours of receipt.
Each case is logged into a centralized Supplier Grievance Management System with a unique reference number.
Investigation & Resolution:

A cross-functional team, including Procurement, Sustainability, and Legal Teams, investigates the issue.
Resolution involves dialogue with the supplier, assessment of evidence, and corrective action planning.
Complex or high-impact grievances are escalated to senior management for review and decision-making.
Standard grievances are resolved within 15 business days.
Critical issues requiring further investigation are addressed as a priority, with interim updates provided to the supplier.
Documentation & Learning:

All resolved grievances are documented, including root cause analysis, corrective actions, and preventive measures.
Lessons learned are integrated into supplier training programs and internal process improvements.

steps.heading: Other Actions Supporting Non-Discriminatory Supply Chain Practices

body.text: Beyond compliance, Skypass Travel advances inclusive sourcing initiatives to empower disadvantaged groups and strengthen community impact. Supporting actions include:

Local ecosystem development, prioritizing procurement from community-based, small-scale, and rural entrepreneurs.
Business partnership and mentorship programs that create equitable tender access and encourage diverse suppliers to participate in competitive bidding without unfair barriers.
Integrating ethical behavior, employee well-being, and social impact metrics into supplier performance evaluations, moving beyond pricing-based selection.

narrative.text:
Quarterly reports summarize the number of grievances, resolution timelines, recurring issues, and preventive measures.
Supplier grievance trends are analyzed to identify systemic risks and drive continuous improvements in supplier engagement and compliance.

Supplier compliance with ESG and DEI requirements is monitored through quarterly audit reviews and annual performance evaluations.
Key KPIs such as percentage of diverse suppliers engaged, audit compliance results, grievance resolution time, and training completion rates are tracked and reported to leadership.
Findings are reviewed during quarterly ESG Committee meetings to identify improvement areas and update sourcing strategies.
Supplier policies, contracts, and the Supplier Code of Conduct are reviewed annually or upon regulatory changes to ensure alignment with global standards.

blocks.text: Safeguarding confidential customer and corporate information—including travel itineraries, booking details, financial and payment data, digital identity documents, and other sensitive records is fundamental to maintaining customer trust and meeting international compliance obligations. This Incident Response Plan (IRP) establishes a structured framework to rapidly identify, assess, contain, and resolve cybersecurity incidents or data breaches affecting Skypass Travel Group operations across all global offices. The plan ensures operational continuity, regulatory compliance, and protection of customer, employee, and partner data.
The primary objectives of this IRP are to:

Ensure rapid detection and immediate response to incidents involving confidential or sensitive information.
Limit the damage and operational disruption caused by a security breach.
Fulfill regulatory requirements for breach notification and reporting in applicable jurisdictions.
Enable effective and transparent communication with internal stakeholders, customers, partners, and regulators.
Prevent recurrence through continuous improvement, post-incident analysis, and procedural strengthening.
This plan applies to:

All global offices of Skypass Travel Group, including remote employees and third-party service environments.
All IT systems, digital platforms, cloud infrastructure, and internal communication tools.
Breaches involving personal data, financial information, corporate records, vendor data, or operational systems.
Examples of events covered under this IRP include:

Unauthorized access, disclosure, modification, or theft of customer travel records or payment details.
Loss or compromise of employee data, financial records, or sensitive business information.
Cyberattacks including malware, ransomware, phishing, account takeover, or system hacking.
Insider threats, accidental disclosures, or system misconfigurations.
Failures or security breaches affecting third-party partners handling Skypass data.

responsibilities: Leads and coordinates incident management and response activities across departments.
Detects incidents, performs technical investigation, organizes containment and eradication efforts.
Ensures response compliance with international privacy laws and reporting obligations.
Advises on legal exposure, regulatory obligations, contractual implications, and stakeholder communications.
Manages controlled internal and external communications, including notifications to customers and media.
Assess operational and data impact, support risk evaluation and restoration priorities.
Must report suspected security incidents immediately through approved channels.

body.text: The IRP is activated when any of the following conditions are identified or suspected:

Unauthorized access or attempts to access sensitive systems or data.
Data leakage through email, portable devices, social engineering, or system exposure.
Malware, ransomware, phishing, or unusual network activity suggesting compromise.
Lost or stolen devices (laptops, phones, storage media) containing confidential data.
Discrepancies in system records indicating manipulation, corruption, or fraud.
Reports of suspicious activity from employees, customers, vendors, or partners.
Notification of a breach from a third-party vendor or cloud service provider.
Abnormal system behavior or unexplained performance spikes.

narrative.text:
All Skypass personnel must stay alert to security anomalies, suspicious emails, unusual account activity, or system performance issues.
Suspected or confirmed incidents must be reported immediately via:
Internal incident reporting portal
Security hotline or emergency contact number
Directly to the IT Security Lead or Incident Response Team
A reporter must provide:
Time and method of detection
Description of suspected breach
Systems, users, or data that may be affected
Any actions already taken

blocks.text: Incidents will be categorized based on severity and potential impact:

rows: Large-scale breach impacting sensitive personal data, financial records, or operational service disruption with regulatory or reputational consequences.
Limited data exposure or partial disruption with moderate operational or compliance risk.
Minor or isolated incidents with minimal business or customer impact. Handled through routine corrective actions and monitoring.

blocks.text: Severity classification determines urgency, escalation requirements, and resource allocation.

body.text: The first individual who identifies a breach must:

Treat all suspicions as urgent—no incident is too minor to report.
Take reasonable steps to contain exposure without altering any system evidence, such as:
Disconnect affected devices from the network.
Disable compromised user accounts and force password resets.
Stop system processes causing visible data leakage.
Report the incident immediately to the Incident Response Team.
Document key initial information including date/time, observations, affected systems, and steps taken.
Avoid deleting files, modifying system configurations, or conducting self-investigation.

The IRT isolates compromised systems, networks, accounts, or applications.
System logs, event records, and device evidence are secured for forensic review.
Temporary protection measures may be applied (e.g., email shutdown, IP blocking, access restrictions).
All actions taken are fully recorded.

IT Security conducts root-cause analysis and forensic review.
Scope and data affected are identified.
Potential harm to customers or business continuity is assessed.
External cybersecurity professionals may be engaged for advanced forensics.
Legal & Compliance determine mandatory reporting obligations under applicable regulations such as:

GDPR (EU) – Notification within 72 hours
DPDPA India – Prompt reporting as required
CCPA / U.S. State Breach Laws – Within prescribed timelines
PCI-DSS – Immediate reporting for payment card data exposure
Affected customers, partners, and internal leadership will be notified using approved messaging.
Notifications will include:
Details of the breach
Data compromised
Potential risks
Recommended protective actions
Support services provided (e.g., monitoring assistance)

Removal of malicious elements, closure of vulnerabilities, security patching, and system cleanup.
Restoration of safe system functionality from verified clean backups.
Implementation of enhanced monitoring to detect persistence attempts.

Formal review meeting held within 7–14 days.
A comprehensive incident report is generated including timelines, actions taken, lessons learned, and CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Actions).
Policies, controls, technology tools, and training programs are updated based on findings.
Disciplinary measures applied if negligence or misconduct is confirmed.

blocks.text:
Only authorized personnel may communicate externally regarding the incident.
All messaging will be approved by Legal, Compliance, and Corporate Communications.
Information will be accurate, transparent, and constructed to maintain customer trust and protect Skypass reputation.

Mandatory cybersecurity awareness training for all employees annually.
Periodic simulation exercises (phishing tests, tabletop scenarios).
IRT specialized technical training and readiness reviews.

All incident documentation including logs, timelines, communications, and forensic results will be recorded in the incident management system.
Records will be securely retained in accordance with regulatory requirements, minimum 7 years.
Documentation will be available for audit or regulator review upon request.

sops.title: Responsible Information Management & Data Protection Measures

blocks.text: Skypass Travel is committed to safeguarding confidential information and ensuring proper retention and secure disposal of records. This SOP establishes the guidelines and responsibilities for handling sensitive customer, partner, and operational data, ensuring compliance with legal, regulatory, and operational requirements across all Skypass Travel offices globally.

Obtain explicit stakeholder consent for processing, sharing, and storing confidential customer and travel-related information.
Protect third-party data, including customer travel documents, payment details, and personal information, using robust digital (encryption, multi-factor authentication) and physical security measures.
Maintain a records retention schedule aligned with global travel regulations, tax obligations, and data protection laws.
Ensure transparency by informing customers about data collection, storage, and sharing practices.
Implement internal controls to restrict unauthorized access to sensitive customer and business data.
Review and update data management practices regularly to comply with evolving regulations internationally.
Provide dedicated support channels for customers and partners to resolve data-related queries.
Guarantee secure disposal of records once retention periods expire, in line with global travel industry standards.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party vendors handling confidential travel data, partner information, supplier data, and operational records. It covers digital and physical records, across all office locations, including head offices, branch offices, and remote work arrangements, ensuring compliance with internal policies, GDPR, Indian IT Act, and other applicable international regulations.

responsibilities: Oversees global data strategy and compliance.
Implements data policies and manages retention and audit procedures.
Protects customer communication, consent, and booking data.
Secures reservation data and coordinates with booking platforms.
Manages employee data, consent collection, and privacy training.
Ensures secure handling of financial records and payment information.
Maintains digital security, backups, and secure data transfers.
Manages access to customer data and privacy requests.
Ensures adherence to legal requirements and performs regular data audits.

body.text:
Consent forms clearly state purpose, scope, duration, and legal basis for data processing with airlines, hotels, visa providers, insurance companies, and government authorities.
Forms are written in plain language and multiple regional languages.
Rights such as withdrawal, rectification, erasure, data portability, and complaint filing are clearly communicated.
Separate consent options are available for essential services, marketing, profiling, and loyalty programs.

Consent is collected via online portals, apps, office visits, calls, emails, and partner platforms.
Each consent is recorded with metadata (timestamp, IP address, staff details, version of form) for audit purposes.
Progressive consent mechanisms allow customers to provide basic consent first and additional consent later.
Confirmation mechanisms include email receipts, SMS, and printed acknowledgments.

Consent is tracked through an integrated system connected to CRM and booking databases.
Role-based access controls restrict who can access or modify consent records.
Automated validation checks ensure all data processing activities are authorized.
Detailed audit logs of consent access, changes, and processing are maintained.
Advanced analytics monitor patterns in consent usage to identify potential gaps or misuse.
System generates compliance reports for internal management and external audits automatically.

Scheduled reviews of consent records occur quarterly, semi-annually, and annually.
Customers are notified of changes in policies, practices, or regulations affecting consent.
Automated systems monitor consent expiry and trigger renewal processes in advance.
Personalized reminders are sent to customers before renewal deadlines with clear instructions for updating consent.
Exceptions or special cases (e.g., regulatory consent requirements for specific regions) are flagged for manual review.

Withdrawal options include online, email, phone, or written requests.
Requests are processed within regulatory timelines with documented confirmation.
Partial withdrawals are supported for specific purposes.
Automated confirmation of withdrawal is sent to customers immediately after processing.
Customers are provided with guidance on the consequences of withdrawal (e.g., limited access to certain services).

Customers receive regular updates and detailed transparency reports.
Dedicated support channels address privacy and data queries.
Educational campaigns (emails, videos, webinars) are conducted periodically to enhance customer understanding of data privacy.
FAQs and self-help guides are maintained online to assist customers in managing their consent preferences independently.

narrative.text:
Compliance dashboards provide real-time visibility of consent management.
Regular training and external expert consultations ensure alignment with evolving legal requirements.
Key metrics such as consent opt-in rates, withdrawals, and expirations are tracked and reported to management monthly.
Periodic internal and external audits ensure ongoing compliance with international and regional regulations.

sections.title: Operational Process for Consulting and Informing Stakeholders

body.text:
Customers are provided detailed, clear, accessible, and regularly updated information regarding our travel data handling practices.
Multiple channels are used: company website (dedicated privacy sections), emails with personalized content, booking confirmations with privacy information, and one-on-one travel consultations.
Data collected (passport, financial information, preferences) and its uses (bookings, insurance, personalization) are clearly disclosed.
Communications are available in multiple languages and formats for accessibility.
Regular newsletters or email campaigns highlight updates to privacy policies or changes in data practices.
Customer surveys are conducted to understand information clarity and to gather feedback on privacy communication effectiveness.

Comprehensive documentation is maintained covering all aspects of travel data management: collection, processing, storage, sharing, and disposal.
Accessible in digital and print formats with simplified explanations, flowcharts, and diagrams.
Version control ensures stakeholders always access the latest policy and procedure documents.
Executive summaries and quick-reference guides are provided to facilitate easier understanding for non-technical stakeholders.

Multiple dedicated channels handle questions or concerns regarding travel data handling, privacy practices, or data rights.
Staff receive ongoing training to provide accurate and timely responses regarding consent, data protection, and security.
Support channels include privacy phone lines, email support, live chat, and in-person consultations at offices.
Extended support hours and multilingual support ensure global stakeholder accessibility.
Ticketing systems track all requests and issues to ensure resolution within defined timelines and regulatory compliance.

Regular transparency reports are published, providing proactive and clear updates on data practices.
Updates are shared via email, newsletters, website, and direct stakeholder consultations.
Stakeholders are offered opportunities to engage, ask questions, and provide feedback on privacy practices.
Critical changes to data handling or regulatory requirements trigger immediate notifications to stakeholders.
Stakeholders are informed of audit results or compliance assessments relevant to data management and privacy practices.

Regular engagement sessions (webinars, workshops, or focus groups) are organized to discuss data handling, privacy practices, and service improvements.
Feedback collected is incorporated into updates of data policies, consent processes, and communication strategies.
A formal mechanism exists for stakeholders to escalate unresolved concerns or complaints to senior management.
Surveys and periodic feedback collection help measure stakeholder satisfaction and identify areas for improvement in data handling transparency.

Information shared with stakeholders accounts for local laws, GDPR, and other international privacy standards.
Cross-border data handling and sharing practices are explicitly communicated with any associated risks.
Country-specific privacy notices are provided for stakeholders in international offices to meet local compliance requirements.
Stakeholders are informed of mechanisms to exercise their privacy rights in accordance with local and international regulations.

Multi-layered role-based access controls ensure only authorized personnel access sensitive customer and partner travel data.
Advanced encryption protocols protect data in transit and at rest, including communications with travel partners and government agencies.
Principle of least privilege is enforced, limiting access strictly to what employees need for their roles.
Regular access reviews identify and revoke unnecessary permissions.
All access activities are logged and monitored using advanced Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems.
Automated alerts flag unusual access patterns or attempts to access unauthorized data.
Third-party vendors undergo periodic security assessments before and during engagement to ensure adherence to access control policies.

Sensitive data storage areas, server rooms, customer service zones, and document repositories are access-controlled.
Security measures include biometric authentication, access card systems with individual tracking, CCTV surveillance, and high-security filing cabinets.
Physical security incidents are promptly investigated and escalated per company protocol.
Security audits are conducted regularly to identify vulnerabilities in physical infrastructure.
Visitor management procedures require sign-in, escorting, and documentation of all non-authorized personnel entering secure areas.

Mandatory training ensures staff understand proper handling of sensitive third-party data, including passports, visas, and financial details.
Employees in high-risk roles receive specialized training and refresher sessions.
Continuous monitoring tools flag suspicious behavior, with clear escalation protocols.
Employees sign acknowledgment forms confirming understanding of third-party data responsibilities.
Simulated phishing and data-handling exercises are conducted to reinforce awareness and practical application.

Third-party service providers (e.g., booking platforms, payment processors, travel partners) are required to follow strict data protection agreements.
Security and privacy obligations are contractually enforced and include audits and reporting requirements.
Periodic security and compliance assessments are conducted for all third parties handling sensitive data.
Data sharing with third parties is limited to the minimum required information, with anonymization applied where feasible.

All third-party data transfers use encryption protocols (TLS/SSL) and secure VPN channels.
Digital keys and certificates are managed with strict internal controls.
Data integrity checks are performed during transmission to detect unauthorized changes or tampering.
Sensitive data sent to international offices or external partners undergoes additional scrutiny to comply with cross-border data regulations.

Regular audits ensure compliance with internal policies and legal/regulatory obligations for third-party data protection.
Any suspicious or unauthorized activity is reported immediately to the Incident Response Team (IRT).
Continuous automated monitoring identifies anomalies in access or usage of third-party data.
Third-party breaches or incidents are promptly communicated to stakeholders, with mitigation and remedial actions documented and implemented.

blocks.text:
Policies, procedures, and training are reviewed and updated regularly based on audits, incidents, and evolving regulatory standards.
Best practices from the travel industry and cybersecurity frameworks are incorporated.
Feedback from customers, partners, and internal staff is used to strengthen third-party data protection measures.
Lessons learned from data breaches or near misses inform updates to access controls, encryption standards, and training programs.

sections.title: Internal Controls to Restrict Data Access

body.text:
Multi-factor authentication and role-based access control with regular audits.
Data Loss Prevention (DLP) systems prevent unauthorized data transfers or downloads.
Network Segmentation: Critical systems are separated from general networks to reduce risk of lateral movement in case of compromise.
Automated Alerts: Real-time monitoring systems generate alerts for suspicious login attempts, unusual data access, or bulk downloads.

Verified credentials and biometric systems secure office and IT areas.
Entry logs are reviewed regularly for abnormal access patterns.
Visitor Management: All visitors must be pre-registered, escorted, and logged with purpose, duration, and areas accessed.
Secure Device Policy: Only authorized devices (laptops, USBs, external drives) are allowed in sensitive areas, all logged and monitored.

sops.title: Specific Approval Procedure for Sensitive Transactions

blocks.text: The purpose of this SOP is to establish strict internal controls, ethical standards, and transparent authorization processes to prevent corruption, bribery, fraud, and conflicts of interest in all sensitive financial transactions. This procedure ensures accountability, traceability, and compliance with relevant laws, international anti-corruption standards (e.g., ISO 37001), and company values.
This procedure applies to:

All employees, contractors, consultants, and board members.
All financial and procurement transactions, contracts, and agreements.
All suppliers, service providers, intermediaries, agents, and partners.
Any transaction involving potential legal, financial, reputational, or ethical risk.
Transaction types covered:

High-value purchasing and procurement contracts.
Vendor onboarding, renewals, and subcontracting arrangements.
Third-party agent commissions, advisory fees, and consultancy payments.
Donations, sponsorships, marketing promotions, and political contributions.
Gifts, hospitality, entertainment, or travel benefits.
Cash handling transactions or unusual payment structures (foreign currency, cash advances, crypto, etc.).

rows.definition: Any transaction that has potential corruption, financial loss, or reputational risk
Designated role holder with authority to approve financial commitments.
A personal, financial, or relational interest that could affect impartial decision-making.
Verification and background assessment of suppliers, partners, or transaction legitimacy.

responsibilities: Prepare and submit request with complete documentation and justification.
Verify cost reasonableness, perform financial due diligence, validate documents.
Conduct corruption risk assessment and policy compliance check.
Review approvals, detect anomalies, and conduct audits.
Approve high-risk or high-value transactions not covered under routine delegation limits.

body.text:
All transactions must be reviewed against a Corruption & Sensitive Transaction Risk Matrix evaluating:
Transaction amount
Country/industry risk score
Supplier or partner reputation
Payment method (cash / foreign / advance / non-standard)
Any declared conflict of interest
Transactions meeting defined criteria are flagged as sensitive and routed through enhanced controls.
The requestor must submit a Sensitive Transaction Request Form including:

Business justification and financial impact analysis.
Formal quotation / proposal / contract copy.
Three comparative quotations (where applicable) for transparency.
Vendor due diligence reports (legal verification, sanctions list check, reference checks).
Conflict of Interest Declaration Form.
Compliance screening checklist.
Requests without complete documentation are automatically rejected.
Key rules:

Segregation of Duties (SoD): no employee may request and approve the same transaction.
Sensitive approvals must be documented through digital workflow systems (ERP / e-signing tools).
Verbal or informal approvals are strictly prohibited.

Mandatory checks performed before onboarding:
Legal registration verification
PAN/GST verification / banking validation
AML, sanctions, and PEP list screening
Litigation history review
Ethics and labor compliance status check
Vendors must sign the Anti-Bribery & Corruption Declaration and Supplier Code of Conduct before engagement.
High-risk third parties undergo Enhanced Due Diligence including site visit, reference verification, and compliance questionnaire.

Payments processed only against verified deliverables and approved purchase orders.
Cash transactions above defined limit are prohibited without CEO approval.
Split invoicing or artificially dividing transactions to bypass approval limits is banned.
Commission payments must be performance-based and contract-supported.

All sensitive transaction records must be maintained for a minimum of 7 years.
Documentation stored securely in encrypted digital systems with access controls.
Audit trails must show:
Date of request
Reviewer comments
Final approval
Supporting evidence

Anonymous reporting channel:
Confidential hotline
Secure email
Whistleblower portal
Complaints handled with confidentiality and non-retaliation commitments.
Compliance team conducts investigations and reports findings to management.
Violations may result in:

Written warnings / probation
Suspension or termination
Legal action and referral to authorities
Supplier blacklisting or contract termination
